raw_response:
I will do mostly what has worked for me before, because 3 mu is small and every bag of fertilizer is real money, but I will not cut too hard on fertilizer and risk losing grain. On my land, wheat and maize follow each other, so I will plant wheat on the full 3 mu in the winter season and then maize on the same 3 mu in the summer season. I have well water, so I do not have to depend only on the sky. For wheat, I will put a heavier base fertilizer and then topdress once when it starts standing up strong, because wheat needs feeding early and I do not want weak seedlings or thin heads. For maize, I will still feed it enough, but a little less than wheat, and I will chase fertilizer around the jointing stage when it starts pulling hard. Around here, if neighbors see a dry spell, they water; I do the same, because one missed watering can cost more than one extra trip to the well. I will keep pesticide use to what I usually do, not too many sprays, just enough to stop the obvious disease, worm, or weed problem from getting ahead of me. On my small farm I will use rotary tillage because it is cheaper and faster than deep ploughing, and I can finish on time.
